P3_addition.f_N_note: 0.30 is a conventional nominal effective Higgs-nucleon form factor, not exact; literature quotes values around 0.30 with uncertainties, e.g. f_N=0.308(18).

P4_primary_source.authors: V. V. Nesvizhevsky, G. Pignol, K. V. Protasov
P4_primary_source.title: Neutron scattering and extra-short-range interactions
P4_primary_source.mapping_to_tpl: In the source convention the neutron has unit charge and a nucleus has approximately A nucleon charges. For the Higgs-mixed scalar, the neutron charge is Q_N and a nucleus is approximated as A*Q_N, so the paper's g^2 maps to Q_N^2 at nucleon level.
P4_primary_source.mapping_assumption: Additive nucleon charge; nuclear binding/composition corrections and screening are not included.

preliminary_source_note.finding: The preliminary preprint calls its result an upper limit, but the inequality sign as rendered in Eq. (6) PDF appears as >. This conflicts with the prose 'upper limit' and the excluded-region plot. Do not silently normalize the printed sign; use the later published 2008 analysis and its explicit <= bound as the primary P4 numeric constraint.

model_parameters.interpretation: The user's stated bound is sin(theta) <= 1e-6. Since the predicted g^2 lambda^2 scales as sin(theta)^2, values computed at 1e-6 are the largest within this interval for fixed f_N and m_S.

interpretation.10_eV: lambda approximately 19.73 nm, above this paper's 0.1 nm upper endpoint. OUTSIDE_SOURCE_VALIDITY_RANGE; this neutron limit alone cannot classify it as excluded or not excluded.
interpretation.10_keV: lambda approximately 19.73 pm, inside 1 pm–0.1 nm. Predicted Q_N^2 lambda^2 is approximately 5.10e-10 fm^2, about 3.19e-8 of the 0.016 fm^2 upper limit. NOT_EXCLUDED_BY_THIS_NEUTRON_BOUND at sin(theta)=1e-6; smaller mixing weakens it further.
interpretation.10_MeV: lambda approximately 0.0197 pm, below this paper's 1 pm lower endpoint. OUTSIDE_SOURCE_VALIDITY_RANGE; no inference from this neutron bound.

limitations: The neutron bound uses an additive nucleon-charge approximation; composite nuclear scalar charges require nuclear-structure and binding corrections for precision work.
The bound applies only in the source's stated 1e-12 to 1e-10 m range for Eq. (13).
The quoted 95% CL limit is one experiment/data-analysis constraint, not a global exclusion envelope.
No astrophysical limits or screening model have been included.
The 10 eV and 10 MeV points are outside the Eq. (13) range; OUTSIDE_RANGE is not equivalent to experimentally allowed.
